report_name: Microsoft's Record October Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,413 CVEs, One Exploited Zero-Day

attack_patterns.name: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass
attack_patterns.description: A zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-96951) is actively exploited to bypass the Mark of the Web (MotW) security feature, allowing malicious files to execute without the standard security warnings.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The attack requires user interaction, where a victim is socially engineered into opening a malicious file that exploits CVE-2026-96951.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-96951
vulnerabilities.description: An actively exploited zero-day security feature bypass vulnerability in Windows Shell that allows attackers to bypass the Mark of the Web (MotW) security mechanism. The flaw was added to CISA's KEV catalog.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-108398
vulnerabilities.description: A publicly disclosed security feature bypass vulnerability in the .NET Framework that could allow an attacker to bypass Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policies.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-92707
vulnerabilities.description: A publicly disclosed, moderate-severity Denial-of-Service (DoS) vulnerability in the MessagePack-CSharp binary serialization library.

indicators.name: Suspicious Script Host Execution from Office Application
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Script Host Execution from Office Application
id: 2b9a8c7d-1e2f-4b3c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Office applications spawning suspicious script hosts like powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or mshta.exe. This may indicate exploitation of vulnerabilities that bypass Mark-of-the-Web, such as CVE-2026-96951.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/microsoft-patches-record-1413-vulnerabilities-including-exploited-windows-zero-day/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-15
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1553.005
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powerpnt.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: This indicator detects Microsoft Office applications spawning script hosts, a behavior associated with the exploitation of the Mark of the Web bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-96951.
